name: Familial Isolated Cardiac Conduction Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Familial Isolated Cardiac Conduction Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Progressive atrioventricular or intraventricular conduction block documented on ECG
No evidence of structural heart disease on echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Positive family history of isolated cardiac conduction disease
Identification of pathogenic variant in known associated genes (e.g., SCN5A, LMNA)
Exclusion of secondary causes of conduction disease such as ischemia, myocarditis, or infiltrative cardiomyopathies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive conduction block with absence of structural heart disease and positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

rare.notes: Usually in advanced disease or with arrhythmias

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to cerebral hypoperfusion

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic or inflammatory causes
imaging: Cardiac MRI showing absence of fibrosis or infiltrative disease
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SCN5A, LMNA, or other conduction system-related genes
other: ECG showing progressive conduction delays (e.g., PR prolongation, bundle branch blocks)
Holter monitoring demonstrating intermittent conduction block

distinguishingFeatures: Typically older patients without family history
Presence of structural heart disease on imaging
Systemic signs of infiltrative disorders (e.g., amyloidosis, sarcoidosis)
Regional wall motion abnormalities on imaging

redFlags: Rapid progression to complete heart block
Family history of sudden cardiac death
references: Schott JJ et al. Familial isolated cardiac conduction disease: clinical and genetic features. Circulation. 1999.
Groenewegen WA et al. Genetic basis of progressive cardiac conduction disease. Heart Rhythm. 2018.
Orphanet: Familial isolated cardiac conduction disease. Orphanet Report Series. 2021.
